newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's Neftohim refinery hit by lack of oil.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's Neftohim refinery hit by lack of oil.

text.p: Bulgaria's oil refinery Neftohim, which feeds the biggest part of the domestic market, may run out of oil in a few days if it does not receive new supplies, a refinery official said.
The official, who declined to be named, said a 75,000-tonne tanker has not been unloaded at Bourgas due to irregularities in its documents.

Neftohim's spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said the refinery sold 2,750 tonnes of petrol on Wednesday. The plant produces 15,000 tonnes of petrol per day now compared to 20,000 tonnes at the end of December.
The refinery has 44,000 tonnes of crude on stock, Hadzhieva said. But half of this volume is an obligatory minimum for the installations, trade unions said.
Nation-wide protests have reached the refinery and more than 3,000 workers rallied on Wednesday demanding clarification of the financial situation of the refinery, the local BTA news agency said.
The plant's management agreed last week to increase its workers' wages by 35 percent from January 1 to avert a strike.
However, trade unions threaten to block the plant's exits and its terminal and prevent fuel going to the country except for hospitals and schools.

Neftohim union officials said the plant owed millions of dollars to suppliers, many of whom were no longer delivering. The plant had losses of some 100 billion levs last year and 37 billion levs in January, they said. There was no independent confirmation.

Part of Neftohim's debt is a result from a barter deal, newspapers said. The refinery exported 50,000 tonnes of fuel to Yugoslavia against grain and has received only two billion levs from the Socialist government, they reported.
Union leaders said the state owed the refinery $80 million from the barter deal.

Neftohim officials say the refinery has suffered huge losses because of the drastic collapse of the lev, forcing up the cost of imported crude faster than the rise in Neftohim's domestic sales prices.
The Bulgarian lev traded near 1,500 per dollar on Wednesday amid expectations of a further fall. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
